background: Maximin share is the value an agent can ensure by partitioning goods into n bundles and receiving her least-valued bundle. Exact simultaneous MMS can fail for additive goods, motivating universal approximate guarantees. Algorithmic guarantees and impossibility instances must be stated separately for a fixed n and uniformly over all n.
short_statement: An agent's maximin share is the value of the worst bundle when she optimally partitions all goods into $n$ bundles. Exact MMS allocations need not exist, so what is the largest constant $\alpha$ such that $\alpha$-MMS allocations always exist for additive valuations?
full_statement: There is a set of agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and a set of indivisible goods $M$, with each agent $i$ having a nonnegative additive valuation $v_i$. Let $\Pi_n(M)$ be the set of all partitions of $M$ into $n$ bundles. Agent $i$'s maximin share is $$\mathrm{MMS}_i=\max_{(B_1,\dots,B_n)\in\Pi_n(M)}\ \min_{j} v_i(B_j),$$ i.e., the best value she can guarantee herself if she partitions all goods into $n$ bundles and receives the worst one. An allocation $A=(A_1,\dots,A_n)$ is $\alpha$-MMS if $v_i(A_i)\ge\alpha\cdot\mathrm{MMS}_i$ for all agents $i$. Exact ($\alpha=1$) MMS allocations do not always exist, even with additive valuations. Determine $$\alpha^*=\sup\{\alpha:\ \text{every additive instance admits an }\alpha\text{-MMS allocation}\}.$$ Here the quantifier includes all agent counts; for fixed n write $\alpha_n^*$, so $\alpha^*=\inf_n\alpha_n^*$. The reviewed universal bounds are $7/9\le\alpha^*\le20/21$. The polynomial-time computability of the guarantee is a closely related companion question.
known_results: Huang and Zhou, 'A Strongly Polynomial-Time 7/9-Approximation Algorithm for Maximin Share Allocations' (arXiv:2511.13056v3, November 5, 2026), Theorem 8.1, give a complete $7/9$-MMS allocation in strongly polynomial time, improving $10/13$. Ezra and Garbuz, 'Improved Impossibility Bounds for Maximin Share Allocations' (arXiv:2609.15085v2), Theorem 2, give a four-agent eleven-good instance bounding the universal guarantee by $20/21$. Their Theorem 1 separately gives $\alpha_n^*\le1-\Omega((\log n)^{-2})$ for sufficiently large n. These are nonnegative additive goods with equal entitlements. The sharp universal constant remains between the stated bounds.

where_posed.text: The MMS notion is due to Budish, 'The Combinatorial Assignment Problem: Approximate Competitive Equilibrium from Equal Incomes', JPE 2011. The approximation question was posed by Procaccia and Wang, 'Fair Enough: Guaranteeing Approximate Maximin Shares', EC 2014, extended in Kurokawa, Procaccia, Wang, JACM 2018, after showing exact MMS allocations need not exist.

progress.summary: Both sides improve: a new constructive guarantee and stronger impossibility instances. Fixed-n and universal constants are now separated.

counterexample_rationale: Explicit valuation matrices can improve impossibility bounds. Exact MMS values and all allocations require certificates.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can test hard instances or allocation rules against the updated frontier, but cannot establish general correctness from simulations.

literature.synthesis: The new existence algorithm uses dynamic witness allocations; the new impossibility constructions improve both universal and n-dependent bounds. Neither establishes the optimal universal constant.

reviewed.ref: Kurokawa, Procaccia, Wang, 'Fair Enough: Guaranteeing Approximate Maximin Shares', AAAI 2016 / JACM 2018 (EC 2014)
reviewed.result: Exact MMS allocations need not exist for additive valuations; $2/3$-MMS allocations always exist.

reviewed.ref: Ghodsi, Hajiaghayi, Seddighin, Seddighin, Yami, 'Fair Allocation of Indivisible Goods: Improvements and Generalizations', EC 2018
reviewed.result: $3/4$-MMS allocations always exist for additive valuations; also constants for submodular ($1/3$) and XOS ($1/5$) classes.

reviewed.ref: Garg, Taki, 'An Improved Approximation Algorithm for Maximin Shares', EC 2020 / Artificial Intelligence 2021
reviewed.result: $(3/4+1/(12n))$-MMS allocations exist and are computable in polynomial time, via a simplified valid-reduction framework.

reviewed.ref: Feige, Sapir, Tauber, 'A Tight Negative Example for MMS Fair Allocations', WINE 2021
reviewed.result: Explicit additive instances where no allocation gives all agents more than $1-1/n^4$ times their MMS ($n\ge 4$), and a $39/40$ upper bound for $n=3$.

reviewed.ref: Akrami, Garg, 'Breaking the 3/4 Barrier for Approximate Maximin Share', SODA 2024
reviewed.result: $(3/4+3/3836)$-MMS allocations always exist for additive valuations — first improvement past the $3/4$ barrier.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Use the updated universal interval to set targets. Separate finite hard-instance certificates from all-instance allocation guarantees.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A claimed improved existence guarantee must handle ARBITRARY additive instances and every agent simultaneously; referees should check the reduction steps preserve all agents' MMS values (the classic failure mode: a reduction that lowers a non-removed agent's maximin share), and that ties/degenerate values are handled. A claimed hard instance must specify the full valuation matrix and prove, by exhaustive search or a combinatorial argument, that every partition into $n$ bundles leaves some agent below $\alpha\cdot\mathrm{MMS}_i$ — note that computing each $\mathrm{MMS}_i$ is itself NP-hard, so exact values must be certified (e.g., by exhibiting the optimal partition and a matching upper bound). Small instances are fully machine-checkable.
